newsitem.title: USA: Harris Corp wins major Chilean phone contract.
newsitem.headline: Harris Corp wins major Chilean phone contract.

text.p: The international communications and electronics company Harris Corp has won a contract to help a Chilean telephone company expand its network by more than 65 percent.
Terms of the contract were not disclosed.
Harris said in a statement it would provide digital telephone switches for use by Compaa de Telfonos (CMET), a privately-held company based in Santiago.
The equipment will enable CMET to expand the number of telephone lines it provides in Santiago, Via del Mar and Rancaeua from 60,000 now to 100,000 by next spring.
Latin America is one of the fastest growing markets in the world for telephone and telecommunications services.
Harris, which is based in Melbourne, Florida, last year invested $18 million to take 25 percent of CMET.
CMET plans to use the investment and Harris digital switching technology to expand its telephone network to 500,000 lines by the turn of the century.
